QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_15

question.text: For a SAS-200 sanitation programme delivering toilets to 6,875 households (AB Responsible Services context), the Means of Verification (MoV) for the OUTCOME 'reduction in open defecation' is BEST triangulated through:

answer.text: Photographs of toilets at construction time only

Triangulation of (i) physical inspection of functional toilets, (ii) beneficiary self-report, (iii) village-level Swachh Bharat database check, (iv) school-attendance data (especially girls) as indirect outcome indicator
The SE Managing Director's written confirmation

explanation.text: The Logic: A robust Means of Verification (MoV) design triangulates multiple independent evidence sources: construction output (physical inspection of functional toilets), beneficiary self-report (survey), administrative data (Swachh Bharat database), and a behavioural proxy (school-attendance data, especially for girls). Triangulation across independent sources is the standard sufficiency-of-evidence approach in social-impact assessment. The Trap: Options A, B and D rely on single-source evidence, each with a known weakness — photos prove output not outcome; beneficiary self-report alone is subject to social-desirability bias; an MD's written confirmation is a management representation rather than independent evidence. Note: The specific AB Responsible Services 6,875-household sanitation case and the Swachh Bharat database / school-attendance triangulation are not in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 123-124, 156, 169-173 or 184-193 — the SAS-200 case in the workbook is the ABC Foundation eye-healthcare programme. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of MoV design.
